name: Evolution — Living Population
description: Fig 11b — evolution by natural selection as a genuine place-graph rewrite you can play forward. A `population` (tree[node]) of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes — each carrying a heritable scalar `trait` and a derived `replication_rate` — evolves under an `environment` whose `selection_optimum` DRIFTS over time (a moving target). Every generation the optimum shifts, each cell's replication rate is re-scored by how close its trait sits to the current optimum (a Gaussian fitness kernel), and the fitter cells reproduce: a daughter `cell` node is ADDED to the population with its trait inherited ± Gaussian mutation. Below carrying capacity the population grows; at capacity a Moran-style birth–death evicts the least-fit cell, so the trait cloud keeps chasing the moving optimum instead of freezing. Running it adds/removes place-graph nodes and shifts the optimum leaf each tick — steppable topology for the loom run/animate feature (selection + mutation + reproduction, the minimal Darwinian loop).

drift.description: Shift of the environment's selection optimum per generation (the moving target).

sel_strength.description: Selection sharpness — the Gaussian fitness width (fitness = e^{-s·Δ²}).

mut_sigma.description: Standard deviation of the heritable mutation step passed to each daughter.
